description: Per-directory coverage floors enforced directly in CI from the Cobertura report that
dotnet test produces. These are the only coverage floors this repository has.
Codecov previously held an equivalent set of targets in codecov.yml. It accepted every
upload and processed none of them, leaving each commit in an error state with an empty
report, so it never posted a status and the targets enforced nothing. Both the upload
step and that config were removed rather than left in place looking like a gate.
Each floor sits roughly a point below measured coverage so it ratchets against
regression without blocking current work. Raise a floor when its directory improves.
A floor may be lowered only when covered code is deleted rather than broken: removing
executed-but-meaningless lines drops the ratio without reducing verified behaviour. Any
such change must say what was deleted and why, as the Aerospace entry below does.
Branch percentages are computed from Cobertura condition outcomes, deduplicating
lines that appear under more than one class.

measuredOn.commit: f2f3bce plus the audit evidence gate and the Raptor reference-model cleanup

directories.rationale: Holds the DO-178C and NPR 7150.2 evidence gates. Measured 91.52% line, 75.25% branch.

rationale: Measured 51.81% line, 64.94% branch. Line coverage rose from 21% to 34% once the
engine parameter consistency gate began exercising the concept design declaration
end to end, then to 55.75% when the compliance and readiness audits stopped
asserting their own inputs.
The line floor was then lowered from 54.0, the one place in this file where a floor
has moved down. RaptorEngine.cs carried roughly 280 lines of constructor assignments
-- invented costs, reliability figures, emissions, failure rates, and a fabricated
test and flight history -- every one of which counted as a covered line because
instantiating the class executed it. Deleting that data removed covered lines from
both the numerator and the denominator, so the percentage fell while the amount of
verified behaviour did not change. Propping the ratio back up would have meant
keeping unsourced data about another company's hardware. Branch coverage, which is
the number that tracks decisions rather than declarations, was unaffected.
Largest directory. Measured 56.56% line, 44.77% branch. The rise from 47.33%/34.05%
came from the quality and security audits reading their inputs from AuditEvidence
instead of declaring them inline, which removed a few hundred untested lines.
Measured 28.30% line, 53.33% branch. Branch coverage went from 0% by verifying the
reinforcement-learning controller's value update, reward shaping, and action
dynamics, then rose again when the unreachable quantum and neural-network
scaffolding was deleted rather than documented. The remaining uncovered lines are
generative scaffolding that returns constants after Task.Delay; see
Docs/VERIFICATION_SCOPE.md.
Measured 38.86% line, 44.23% branch. The jump from 30.40%/31.98% is the ideal rocket
nozzle solver, at 100% line and 100% branch coverage across IdealRocketNozzle.cs,
EngineOperatingPoint.cs, and NozzleFlowSolver.cs. The uncovered remainder is the
legacy constant-output solvers; see Docs/VERIFICATION_SCOPE.md.

reason: Models is data-transfer objects with no behaviour. Its 14.42% line coverage is an
incidental by-product of other tests constructing those objects, not evidence of
anything, and 0% branch coverage simply reflects that there are no branches to
cover. A floor here would measure nothing.
